key_insight: The paper introduces ST-VTD, a variational tensor decomposition that combines low-rank spatial structure with learned temporal priors to better separate shared and subject-specific spatiotemporal patterns in multisubject data.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more interpretable and flexible framework for neuroimaging and other spatiotemporal sensing problems where classical tensor models struggle with variability across subjects.
method: Spatial factors are regularized with an LL1-inspired low-rank structure.
Temporal factors use an LSTM-based learned prior to capture adaptive dynamics.
Posterior inference is done with an amortized variational scheme by unrolling optimization iterations, initialized with group ICA warm starts.
evidence_signal: On a realistic synthetic fMRI dataset, the method improved latent factor recovery over representative classical and probabilistic decomposition benchmarks.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the learned temporal prior and warm-start initialization, which may limit robustness outside the tested setting.
paper_title: Variational Low-rank Tensor Decomposition for Multisubject Spatiotemporal Data Analysis
